FACIT-F: 13-item Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy-Fatigue scale (range: 0 to 52 with higher scores indicating less fatigue.). FACIT-F was included in the trial protocol only after patient inclusion had begun (protocol ver. 1.2., approved 19-02-2024) so the FAS for this outcome includes fewer subjects than for other secondary outcomes.
EQ-5D-5L Utility Index: 5-item scale (range: -0.758 to 1 with higher scores indicating better health related quality of life.)
EQ-5D-5L Visual-Analogue Scale: Range: 0 to 100 with higher scores indicating better health related quality of life.
GAF: Global Assessment of Functioning (range: 0-100 with higher scores indicating better functioning.)
SAPS: 34-item Scale for the Assessment of Positive Symptoms (range: 0 to 170 with higher scores indicating more severe psychotic symptoms.)
GTI: 8-item Glucocorticoid Toxicity Index (range: -35 to 410 with higher scores indicating more severe toxicity, modified from original scale to not include the “bone density” item.)
YMRS: 11-item Youngs Mania Rating Scale (range: 0 to 60 with higher scores indicating more severe manic symptoms.)
C-SSRS - Suicidal thoughts: A participant is defined as having suicidal thoughts based on the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) if the participant endorses item 1 and/or 2 on the C-SSRS

C-SSRS - Suicidal ideation: The Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) derived suicidal ideation score (range 0-5) is calculated based on C-SSRS items 1-5, with each item endorsed (“Yes”) adding 1 point to the score

C-SSRS - Suicidal intensity: The Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) derived suicidal intensity score (range 0-25) is calculated based on C-SSRS items 6-10, with each item being scored from 1-5. If participants do not endorse item 1 or 2, the suicidal intensity score is set to 0 (i.e., no suicidal thoughts present)

Analysis is a Mixed Model for Repeated Measurements for post-baseline measurements with main effects of treatment and baseline outcome nested within visit using an unstructured visit-by-visit within-subjects residual variance-covariance matrix. Denominator degrees of freedom for _t_ and _F_ statistics are calculated using Satterthwaite's method.

One-way tipping point analysis in which an adjustment ($\delta$) is applied to the mean outcome of subjects with missing values in each arm separately with no penalty applied in the other arm. The figure shows the estimated treatment difference (Dexamethasone - Placebo) and its 95% CI for a range of $\delta$ values applied separately in each arm. A positive $\delta$ in the active arm or a negative $\delta$ in the placebo arm acts in the conservative direction, i.e., against the hypothesis of a beneficial treatment effect.

Two-way tipping point analysis in which adjustments $\delta_{\text{Dexamethasone}}$ and $\delta_{\text{Placebo}}$ are applied to the mean outcome of subjects with missing values in each arm simultaneously. The contour plot shows the upper 95% confidence limit of the estimated treatment difference (ETD, Dexamethasone - Placebo) across a grid of $\delta$-values. The black solid contour highlights the values of ($\delta_{\text{Dexamethasone}}, \delta_{\text{Placebo}}$) at which the upper 95% CI equals zero, i.e., where the ETD tips between significance and non-significance. A positive $\delta_{\text{Dexamethasone}}$ and a negative $\delta_{\text{Placebo}}$ act in the conservative direction, i.e., against the hypothesis of a beneficial treatment effect.
